What if the ddos attack makes Voat look much more popular?
Ok wait this a good question. Does a DDoS attack make a website look like it has millions of unique visitors when really it is just a bot?
In theory one would think the stats are filtered for such things. But maybe not. Awaiting someone with more knowledge.

Yeah right? I was thinking oh that's awesome that we're trending higher than Reddit on Google trends we must have.. a.... ton... of.... oh crap.

However if those statistics are driving folks away from Reddit perhaps the DDOS is like a jumpstart to popularity! Self fulfilling prophecy. By the time the traffic is real Voat will be ready for it!
I like your optimism! I surely hope so

What I suspect it would boil down to from an analysis and logistics perspective is whether the potential beneficial results of the DDoS in terms of increased popularity and traffic outweigh the negative costs. On the plus side it could increase your claim for traffic, and the DDoS has garnered attention through news, social media, and blog outlets reporting on it which typically drive users toward a site. On the flip side you need to take into account how many users may be lost due to frustration with the site being down (or inaccessible from apps) as well as the overhead costs incurred to mitigate the DDoS (Cloudflare, added bandwidth, and added server hardware sure ain't cheap).
All good points. Voat is looking awfully similar to pied piper.

I was annoyed at first when Boats wouldn't work, but that was also how I learned that the site was being attacked. Hopefully people will properly direct their frustration towards the attackers rather than Voat. On the plus side, I have to say that I'm impressed with how well the mobile version of Voat works. It is quite usable, so I haven't felt too inconvenienced by the DDoS.

Agreed. We should all remember that Reddit certainly went through its own struggles and growing pains early on and was intermittently knocked down due to traffic surges and DDoS attacks. All-in-all I'd say that Voat has managed to handle it all pretty well. I am a software engineer and also handle a lot of devops and cloud infrastructure so I understand the struggles and sympathize with those working their ass off to keep Voat up and running, and I, too, hope everyone else is mindful of the struggles and costs associated with all of this.

Also - the standard desktop and mobile versions of this site are definitely very well done so I also don't feel that I'm missing much by losing access to Boats. But I still would like to see it restored for the app developers who have/are investing time to improve what is already a pretty solid app.
